title: 第21章 伙房之外 中第22章 伙房之外 下
slug: 修仙开局一部手机修为全靠买
content_zh:
他说完这番话，不等刘叙白回答，转身朝寒潭谷的方向走去，走出几步之后，头也不回地扔下最后一句：“她保不了你一辈子。伙房晚上危险多，刘公子小心脚下。”
刘叙白站在伙房前的空地上，目送着韩知渊的身影消失在小路尽头的黑暗中。夜风从他背后灌过来，吹得他的袍角猎猎作响。他把空水囊重新挂回腰间，没有去伙房，也没有马上离开，而是站在原地，把刚才的所有细节都在脑子里过了一遍。
韩知渊说“伙房晚上危险多”的时候，语气里有一种意味深长的暗示，绝不仅仅是虚张声势这么简单。
他低头看了看脚下的碎石地面。月光很淡，地上的碎石被踩得乱七八糟，新旧脚印交错重叠，很难分辨。但他还是找到了他想要的东西——小路边上有一小块被踩碎的冰，冰碴子还很新，边缘尖锐，没有被风吹化过的痕迹。而那块碎冰的位置离伙房后门很近。就在他来这里之前不久，有人从伙房后门出去，踩碎了这块冰，沿着小路往寒潭谷的方向走了。而从后门出去这个方向，恰好避开了韩知渊堵在正门小路的位置。
小蝉不在伙房里。或者说，她在这里，但今晚不在了。
刘叙白没有多做停留。他沿着原路返回，穿过松林，爬上石阶，回到客院的时候已经是深夜了。推开房门，屋里和他离开时一样，被褥整齐，茶壶里的水已经凉透了。他关好门窗，走到露台上往外看了一眼——露台下方的雪地上，又多了一行新鲜的脚印。从他离开客院不久之后就来过，在他回来之前刚走。
韩知渊的眼线。
刘叙白把露台的门关严，回到屋里，在床沿上坐下来。他解开腰间那把苏清欢给的青鞘长剑，轻轻拔出半截。剑身上的青光在黑暗里微微流转，带着一层淡淡的凉意。他把剑重新归鞘，放在床头触手可及的位置，然后没有犹豫，直接掏出手机，点开墟市，找到加入收藏夹的那枚残损剑意石。拇指毫不犹豫地按下了购买键。
三十枚下品灵石从余额中扣除，一枚指甲盖大小的灰扑扑晶石落入掌心。晶石入手冰凉，比同体积的冰块还要冷上几分，里面混沌不清的灰色雾气在缓缓翻滚，像是封着一团没有成型的风暴。
刘叙白握着剑意石盘腿坐下，将意识沉入其中。时间无声流逝，他缓缓睁开眼睛，眉头微皱。脑海中多了一些破碎的剑道感悟碎片，像是有人在他记忆深处贴了几张撕碎的字条，上面的字迹模糊难辨，但隐隐约约能辨认出几个关键词——“意在剑先”“势从地起”“斩……”后面的字被撕掉了。
剑意残片。正如标注所言，感悟没有完全成功——剩余信息太过破碎，无法形成完整的剑意传承。但他隐隐有一种感觉，这残损剑意与他所修的《悟道剑诀》契合度很高，有第一次的经验，往后若再遇到类似的剑意石，或许就能一举破境。他将获得的感悟在心底反复回溯，确认没有遗漏之后，才在床上盘腿入定，照常运转灵力走了一个小周天。
他没有因为今晚被韩知渊截住而气馁。恰恰相反，韩知渊亲自出面堵他，反倒印证了一件事——小蝉这条线索绝对有料，值得对方如此紧张。
第二天一早，刘叙白照常去藏经阁看书。他花了整整一上午翻遍了第一层所有关于画梅宗历史的玉简，在一本不起眼的旧卷宗里找到了一个有用的信息——画梅宗的内务堂卷宗条例规定，所有正式弟子的丹药配给记录，无论批次大小，都必须由药库管事、炼丹房、送药人三方签章，原始存根保存十年不得销毁。这条规定是画梅宗祖师爷立下的，两脉分治也无法更改。
也就是说，苏清欢当初那批筑基丹的原始存根，现在还在。只要找到存根，比对签章，就能锁定当初动手脚的人。
刘叙白把这个发现默默记在心里，打算晚上去找苏清欢的时候告诉她。中午他去了一趟医舍，陈砚今天拆了夹板，正在大夫的指导下做恢复运动。左臂活动起来还有些僵硬，握力也大不如前，但骨头已经长好了，剩下的只是时间问题。阿宁也在，她端着一碗刚熬好的药汤站在床边，看到刘叙白进来，圆圆的脸上浮起一个腼腆的笑容。
“刘大哥。”
“辛苦你了。”刘叙白朝她点了点头，在床边坐下，压低声音对陈砚说，“砚子，有件事要你帮忙。”
陈砚立刻停下了活动手臂的动作，神色一正：“你说。”
“你在医舍养伤的这段时间，顺便帮我留意一下通往寒潭谷方向的路上有什么动静。你现在是伤患，又是外来的散修，不会有人特别提防你。如果看到什么异常——比如夜里有人频繁进出医舍附近的药库，或者有寒潭谷的弟子来医舍探病时打听什么，都帮我记下来。”
陈砚点了点头，没有多问一个字。跟刘叙白相处这么久，他已经学会了不在不合适的时候刨根问底。他只是用没受伤的右手拍了拍胸脯：“放心。”

离开医舍之后，刘叙白又去了一趟藏经阁。他把昨天没看完的几本关于画梅宗内部管理制度的玉简全部翻了一遍，又找到了一本署名“前代流云峰执事笔记”的旧手札，里面详细记录了宗门内部各种案件的处理流程，包括证据保全、证人保护、以及两脉之间的互不越界条款。他把关键信息用纸笔记了下来。
临近傍晚时分，他朝苏清欢的院子走去。他要把今天查到的东西告诉她，也要把昨晚韩知渊截他的事说清楚。他不打算瞒她——在这种地方，信息不透明比任何敌人都危险。
走到半山腰石阶拐角处时，他忽然听见上方传来一道略显耳熟的声音。
“刘叙白？”
抬头一看，是那个叫叶凝的女弟子。她夹着一摞卷宗从石阶上跑下来，脸上还是那副开朗的模样，但这次她的表情里多了一丝凝重。她在刘叙白面前停下，喘了口气，然后左右看了看，确认四下无人之后压低声音说了一句话。
“江长老让我私下给你带句话——苏师妹之前那批筑基丹的事，有人正式向执法堂提出了重查申请。申请人是苏师妹本人，江长老亲自副署的。今天早上递交上去的。”

After he said these words, without waiting for Liu Xubai's reply, he turned around and walked in the direction of Hantan Valley. After taking a few steps, he dropped the last sentence without looking back: "She can't protect you forever. There are many dangers in the kitchen at night, Mr. Liu, be careful where you step."
Liu Xubai stood in the open space in front of the kitchen, watching Han Zhiyuan's figure disappear into the darkness at the end of the path. The night wind came from behind him, making the corners of his robe rustle. He hung the empty water bag back on his waist. He did not go to the kitchen, nor did he leave immediately. Instead, he stood there and went through all the details in his mind.
When Han Zhiyuan said, "The kitchen is more dangerous at night," there was a meaningful hint in his tone, and it was more than just a bluff.
He looked down at the gravel beneath his feet. The moonlight was very faint, the gravel on the ground was trampled into a mess, and the old and new footprints overlapped, making it difficult to distinguish. But he still found what he wanted - a small piece of broken ice on the side of the path. The ice was still new, with sharp edges and no signs of being blown away by the wind. The location of the broken ice was very close to the back door of the kitchen. Not long before he came here, someone went out from the back door of the kitchen, stepped on the ice, and walked along the path towards Hantan Valley. Going out from the back door happened to avoid Han Zhiyuan blocking the main entrance path.
Xiaochan is not in the kitchen. In other words, she is here, but not here tonight.
Liu Xubai didn't stay much. He returned along the original path, passed through the pine forest, climbed up the stone steps, and returned to the guest house late at night. Pushing open the door, the room was the same as when he left. The bedding was neat and the water in the teapot was completely cold. He closed the doors and windows, walked to the terrace and took a look - there was another line of fresh footprints on the snow below the terrace. He had been here not long after he left the guest house, and just before he came back.
Han Zhiyuan's eyeliner.
Liu Xubai closed the balcony door tightly, returned to the room, and sat down on the edge of the bed. He untied the green sheath sword Su Qinghuan gave him from his waist and gently pulled out half of it. The green light on the sword circulated slightly in the darkness, bringing with it a faint coolness. He sheathed the sword again and placed it within reach on the bedside. Then without hesitation, he took out his cell phone, clicked on the market, and found the damaged sword intention stone that he had added to his favorites. The thumb pressed the buy button without hesitation.
Thirty low-grade spiritual stones were deducted from the balance, and a dusty crystal the size of a fingernail fell into the palm of his hand. The crystal was cold to the touch, a bit colder than an ice cube of the same volume. The chaotic gray mist inside was slowly rolling, like an unformed storm sealed inside.
Liu Xubai sat down cross-legged while holding the Jianyi Stone, sinking his consciousness into it. Time passed silently, and he slowly opened his eyes and frowned slightly. There were some broken pieces of kendo insights in his mind, as if someone had pasted a few torn notes deep in his memory. The handwriting on them was blurry and difficult to read, but a few keywords could be vaguely discerned - "Intention is the sword first", "Strength rises from the ground", "Cut..." The following words were torn off.
Fragments of sword intent. As the label said, the enlightenment was not completely successful - the remaining information was too fragmented to form a complete inheritance of sword intention. But he had a vague feeling that this damaged sword intention was very consistent with the "Sword Art of Enlightenment" he had cultivated. With this first experience, if he encounters a similar sword intention stone in the future, he might be able to break through it in one fell swoop. He reviewed the insights he had gained in his heart over and over again, and after confirming that he had not missed anything, he crossed his legs on the bed and fell into meditation, and walked for a small week as usual using his spiritual power.
He was not discouraged by being intercepted by Han Zhiyuan tonight. On the contrary, Han Zhiyuan personally intervened to block him, which confirmed one thing - Xiaochan's clue was definitely informative and worthy of the other party's nervousness.
Early the next morning, Liu Xubai went to the Sutra Pavilion to read as usual. He spent the whole morning looking through all the jade articles on the history of Hua Mei Zong on the first floor.Jane found a piece of useful information in an inconspicuous old file - the Huamei Sect's Internal Affairs Hall File Regulations stipulate that all elixir distribution records for official disciples, regardless of batch size, must be signed by the medicine warehouse manager, the alchemy room, and the person who delivered the medicine. The original stub shall be kept for ten years and shall not be destroyed. This rule was established by the ancestor of Huamei Sect, and it cannot be changed even if the two branches are divided.
In other words, the original stubs of Su Qinghuan's original batch of Foundation Establishment Pills are still there. As long as you find the stub and compare it with the signature, you can identify the person who did it in the first place.
Liu Xubai kept this discovery in mind and planned to tell Su Qinghuan when he went to see her at night. He went to the hospital at noon. Chen Yan had his splint removed today and was doing recovery exercises under the guidance of the doctor. The left arm is still a little stiff when moving, and the grip strength is not as good as before, but the bones have grown, and the rest is only a matter of time. Aning was also there. She was standing by the bed with a bowl of freshly brewed medicinal soup. When she saw Liu Xubai come in, a shy smile appeared on her round face.
"Brother Liu."
"Thank you for your hard work." Liu Xubai nodded towards her, sat down by the bed, and lowered his voice and said to Chen Yan, "Yanzi, I need your help with something."
Chen Yan immediately stopped moving his arms and straightened his expression: "You tell me."
"While you are recuperating in the hospital, help me pay attention to any movement on the road leading to Hantan Valley. You are an injured person now and a casual cultivator from outside, so no one will be particularly wary of you. If you see anything unusual - for example, someone frequently enters and exits the medicine warehouse near the hospital at night, or if disciples from Hantan Valley come to the hospital to inquire about something, write it down for me."
Chen Yan nodded and didn't ask another word. After spending so much time with Liu Xubai, he has learned not to ask questions at inappropriate times. He just patted his chest with his uninjured right hand: "Don't worry."
After leaving the hospital, Liu Xubai went to the Tibetan Scripture Pavilion again. He went through all the jade slips he had not read yesterday about the internal management system of Hua Mei Sect, and found an old handbook signed "Notes of the former Deacon Liu Yunfeng", which recorded in detail the handling process of various cases within the sect, including evidence preservation, witness protection, and non-crossing clauses between the two sects. He wrote down key information on paper.
As evening approached, he walked towards Su Qinghuan's yard. He wanted to tell her what he found out today, and he also wanted to explain clearly what happened to Han Zhiyuan when he intercepted him last night. He wasn't going to hide it from her - in a place like this, opaque information was more dangerous than any enemy.
When he reached the corner of the stone steps halfway up the mountain, he suddenly heard a slightly familiar voice coming from above.
"Liu Xubai?"
When he looked up, he saw the female disciple named Ye Ning. She ran down the stone steps with a stack of files under her arm, her face still looking cheerful, but this time there was a hint of solemnity in her expression. She stopped in front of Liu Xubai, took a breath, then looked around to make sure there was no one around and then said something in a low voice.
"Elder Jiang asked me to leave you a message in private - regarding Junior Sister Su's previous batch of Foundation Establishment Pills, someone formally submitted a re-examination application to the Law Enforcement Hall. The applicant was Junior Sister Su herself, and Elder Jiang personally countersigned it. It was submitted this morning."
